memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"This is how you are to eat it: with your cloak tucked into your belt, your
sandals on your feet and your staff in your hand. Eat it in haste; it is the
LORD's Passover." - Ex 12:11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is not a leisurely dinner. Cloak tucked in, shoes on, staff in hand. They
were to eat like people ready to walk out the door.

Consider what that required. They had been slaves in Egypt for four hundred
years. Every one of them had been born there. Their homes, however poor, were
the only homes they knew. And now God says: eat with your shoes on.

That posture was faith. Nothing had changed yet when they sat down to eat.
Pharaoh had not released them. But God said they were leaving, so they dressed
for the journey.

The New Testament calls believers "foreigners and exiles" here (1 Pet 2:11). We
are not meant to settle so deeply into this world that we could not leave it
gladly. That does not mean neglecting our work, our families, or our
responsibilities. It means holding them with an open hand, knowing our real home
is elsewhere.

Are your shoes on? Not in the sense of being restless or careless about this
life, but in the sense of being ready. Ready to go where God sends. Ready to
release what He asks for. Ready for the day He calls us home.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What are you holding so tightly that you could not leave it if God asked?
2. Does your life show that you expect something better ahead?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, help me to live with my shoes on, holding this world loosely and staying
ready for whatever You call me to. Amen.
